messages:
Sara: quick follow-up on the service auth RFC — we need to pick a practical path for revocation and offline verification. TL;DR: tradeoffs between short-lived signed tokens (no central check) vs long-lived API keys + revocation list (central check). Thoughts?

Omar: +1 to revisiting. My instinct is short-lived JWTs minted by a token service. Advantages: no per-request introspection, easy to verify at edge via JWKs. Drawback: revocation is eventual unless you rotate keys frequently or check a blacklist for high-risk ops.

Linda: Agree with Omar's baseline, but we can't ignore the customer requirement for immediate revoke for compromised keys (enterprise). Need a hybrid.

Kevin: Proposal: hybrid flow:
- Customer holds a long-lived API key (good for provisioning only).
- Token service mints short-lived access tokens (1-5m) when presented the API key.
- API key revocation prevents minting new tokens; token expiry bounds exposure.
- For long-running jobs, provide a refresh-token-like flow with rotation + short refresh windows (and strong audit).

Linda: That covers most cases. Also: embed token_id/jti in the token so we can audit and optionally blacklist a token immediately if needed.

Sara: On RBAC scoping: do we prefer org/project IDs in claims or coarse 'scopes'?

Omar: Put canonical identifiers (org_id, project_id) in claims + a small set of scopes. Reason: downstream services often need org/project for tenancy routing; avoids extra DB call to translate scope -> project.

Kevin: Implementation notes: edge proxies verify signature + exp only. For write/delete/sensitive endpoints do an introspection call to token service (or hit a fast in-memory revocation cache).

Linda: Audit/tracing: token should carry token_id and minted_by client_id, and optionally delegated_by when service A acts on behalf of user B. That lets us link events to the originating API key for compliance.

Omar: Caching JWKs is fine (standard). For immediate revocation we can publish a small delta blacklist for sensitive flows; keep it limited so edge performance isn't impacted.

Kevin: Perf tradeoffs: introspection per-request is expensive and increases P99 latency — prefer an allowlist/denylist in front of sensitive endpoints. Non-sensitive reads: offline verify via JWKs.

Sara: SDK ergonomics: client libs should manage API key -> token exchange automatically, handle refresh and exponential backoff on 401, surface clear errors for revoked keys. Docs should show migration from existing long-lived keys to this hybrid model.

Linda: Security ops: we also need a rotation plan for JWKs with overlap window and clear docs for customers running private deployments.

Kevin: Minimal prototype scope: minting service + short token format + refresh flow + revoke API + edge verification docs.

auth-bot: Ticket created: AUTH-523 "Short-lived tokens + key revocation + refresh flow (MVP)". Assignee: Kevin. Due: 2w.

Sara: Owners: Kevin -> minting & SDK, Linda -> audit schema & revocation API, Omar -> JWK rotation + edge guidance. I'll draft the RFC update tonight and attach a diagram.

Kevin: I'll start a lightweight PoC this afternoon.

Sara: One tiny example token claim set for reference:
```
{
  "iss": "https://auth.redwood.internal",
  "kid": "rot1-2026-03-20",
  "sub": "svc:ingester-3",
  "token_id": "tk_Abc123",
  "org_id": "org_99",
  "project_id": "proj_23",
  "scopes": ["model:invoke","logs:write"],
  "exp": 1710000010
}
```

And a tiny pseudo-introspection for sensitive ops:
```
POST /introspect
Authorization: Bearer <management-token>
{ "token_id": "tk_Abc123" } -> {"active": true, "revoked": false, "reason": null}
```

Sara: ok — thanks all. I'll post the RFC update and link AUTH-523.
